Key Research Thinking Patterns: Hardware-Software Co-Design for Real-Time Metabolic Phenotyping: Integrating handheld dual-excitation frequency-domain FLIM endoscopy with FPGA-based signal processing to enable label-free, real-time assessment of mitochondrial metabolism (NAD(P)H/FAD) for in vivo oral cancer diagnosis.

Multimodal Deep Learning for Enhanced Diagnostic Accuracy: Combining pseudo-color image augmentation and U-Net segmentation with VGG16 transfer learning to improve benign versus malignant mass classification and automated segmentation in full-field digital mammography.

Algorithmic Fairness and Bias Auditing in Medical AI: Implementing fairness gap metrics and tissue-specific fine-tuning strategies to identify and mitigate performance disparities across patient cohorts, ensuring equitable diagnostic outcomes in computational pathology.

Rigorous Statistical Validation of Imaging Biomarkers: Utilizing leave-one-patient-out cross-validation, paired one-tailed t-tests, and Bland-Altman analysis to validate the clinical reliability of metabolic redox ratios and morphological features against gold-standard TCSPC and histopathology.
Summary Description: Javier A. Jo specializes in biomedical engineering, bridging biophotonics and computational diagnostics to advance early cancer detection. His research integrates handheld dual-excitation frequency-domain FLIM endoscopy with FPGA-based real-time processing for label-free metabolic phenotyping of oral lesions. Concurrently, he develops advanced computer-aided diagnosis (CADx) systems for breast cancer, leveraging pseudo-color augmentation, U-Net segmentation, and transfer learning to enhance mass classification. A key focus is ensuring equitable clinical AI deployment through rigorous bias analysis and fairness metrics. By combining hardware-enabled metabolic imaging with sophisticated deep learning frameworks, his work provides robust solutions for surgical margin delineation, intraoperative guidance, and non-invasive screening across multiple anatomical sites.
